body.target_estimand: The primary binary estimand is \(\tau_N=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)\}=(p-q)/n\). For the bounded-class corollary, a schedule \(\mathbf y=(y_{i1},y_{i0})_{i=1}^n\in[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]^{2n}\) has causal ATE \(\tau(\mathbf y)=n^{-1}\sum_i(y_{i1}-y_{i0})\); on the binary endpoint embedding \(y_{id}=L_{\mathrm{bd}}+\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}Y_i(d)\), it satisfies \(\tau(\mathbf y)=\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}\tau_N\)
body.estimand_functional: The primary binary fixed-design functional is \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}=\min_t\max_{N\in\mathcal N_n}\sum_{x,y}K_N(x,y)\{t(x,y)-\tau_N\}^2\). For every fixed assignment law \(\delta\), the bounded-cube minimax ATE functional equals \(\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2\) times its labeled binary-endpoint fixed-design minimax functional. In particular, under uniform balanced complete randomization, \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{bal}}[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]=\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}\) for every positive even \(n\). The globally optimized comparator \(\mathfrak R_n^\star[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]\) additionally takes an infimum over all assignment designs and all measurable estimators.

sampling_model.design: Uniform assignment over \(\mathcal Z_n\), the assignments treating exactly \(m=n/2\) units.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) labeled units and both binary potential outcomes are fixed; the assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: One binary treatment with exactly \(m\) treated and \(m\) controls.
sampling_model.overlap: Every labeled exactly balanced assignment has probability \(1/\binom n m\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no stochastic nuisance estimation; nature ranges over the finite response-type state space \(\mathcal N_n\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Complete randomization is conjectured to remain strictly suboptimal for general estimators uniformly in population size.
``For binary potential outcomes, we show this minimax risk is equivalent to the minimax risk of an estimation problem with \(2\) unknown parameters.''
``A new proof of this result is given, and the restriction to experiments with a finite number of outcomes is removed.''
``This paper shows the minimax optimality of the complete randomization scheme under permutation invariance.''

body.tldr: Exact balance removes treatment-share variation but leaves two observed arm-success counts. For fixed binary potential outcomes, the full pair and its difference have equal worst-schedule ATE squared-error minimax risk at \(n=2,4,6\), but a rational two-sided full-count bracket and a difference-only lower certificate prove strict loss at \(n=8\). A tensor-product endpoint extension separately proves that, for any fixed assignment law, bounded-cube minimax ATE risk equals \(\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2\) times the corresponding labeled binary-endpoint minimax value. Thus balanced complete randomization has exact bounded-cube risks \(\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2/4\), \(\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2(1-\sqrt3/2)\), and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2s_6^2\) at two, four, and six, and a certified \(\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2[C_8,U_8]\) bracket at eight; it is strictly worse than Hull's globally optimized independent design at all four sizes. Later-even compression persistence, the exact eight-unit value, Hull's uniform strictness conjecture, and all asymptotic laws remain open.

project_justification.gap: Published minimax analyses establish the all-design shifted-binomial reduction and report numerical evidence that complete randomization remains strictly suboptimal with general estimators, but do not give exact endpoint certificates for that strict comparison. They also do not locate the first finite size at which compressing the two exact-balance success counts to their difference loses minimax information.
project_justification.niche: The fixed-half binary response-type hypergeometric experiment supplies exact primal-dual certificates, while its binary endpoint embedding supplies rigorous lower bounds for the full bounded schedule class without claiming a nonbinary two-count reduction.
project_justification.fill: The project gives analytic equality saddles at \(n=2,4,6\), rational lower and upper full-count certificates and strict count-compression separation at eight, and a fixed-design tensor-product endpoint theorem equating bounded-cube minimax risk with the scaled labeled binary-endpoint value. The latter yields exact balanced-design bounded risks at two, four, and six, a certified bracket at eight, and strict comparison with Hull's globally optimized independent design at those four sizes.

body.related_work: Hull (2026, Theorem 1 and Appendix A.4) optimizes worst-case ATE squared error jointly over all bounded schedules, assignment designs, and measurable estimators, proves that independent half assignment attains the shifted-binomial minimax program, and uses Bernstein extension plus separate convexity to lift endpoint risks to the full bounded cube. Corollary 1 gives the affine independent-design risk \(\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2/(\sqrt n+1)^2\); footnote 12 records uniform strict suboptimality of complete randomization with general estimators as a conjecture supported numerically. Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\mbox{-}design\mbox{-}endpoint\mbox{-}reduction}\) gives a distinct fixed-design minimax-value equality by extending the complete labeled binary rule, without asserting a nonbinary orbit statistic. Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}hull\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}complete\mbox{-}randomization\mbox{-}strict\mbox{-}small\mbox{-}n}\) combines that equality with finite certificates to prove Hull's strict comparison only for \(n=2,4,6,8\), leaving the uniform conjecture open. Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) study the unrestricted independent-design scalar program and its Airy expansion, not the exact balanced hypergeometric count-compression threshold. Ding and Dasgupta (2016) supply the binary response types and observed table used in the finite kernel. Blackwell (1953) gives only weak dominance of the full count pair over its difference. Bai (2023) treats permutation-invariant linear procedures. Rigdon and Hudgens (2015), Li and Ding (2016), and Li and Ding (2017) concern exact confidence sets or first-order finite-population limits and do not imply the point-estimation or bounded-design claims here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The rational full-count certificates at \(n=8\) prove only \(C_8\leq\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}\leq U_8\), with \(C_8<U_8\), so the exact binary and bounded-cube balanced minimax values remain unknown. An arbitrary prior can make the second count Bayes-informative even where the minimax values agree. The fixed-design endpoint result is an equality of minimax values obtained by tensor-product extension of a full labeled binary rule; it does not prove that two counts, or any other binary orbit statistic, suffice for nonbinary schedules.
body.honest_scope: The theorem-level scope consists of the exact binary response-type games, equality of full-count and difference-only risks at \(n=2,4,6\), strict count-compression separation and a two-sided full-count bracket at \(n=8\), the resulting first-lossy-size conclusion, the fixed-design endpoint minimax-value reduction, exact bounded-cube balanced risks at two, four, and six, a bounded-cube bracket at eight, and strict suboptimality of balanced complete randomization relative to the globally optimized design at those four sizes. The paper makes no confidence-set claim, pointwise-dominance claim, exact \(\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}\) claim, or nonbinary two-count sufficiency claim. Strict count-compression persistence for even \(n\geq10\), Hull's uniform complete-randomization conjecture, and every asymptotic rate, exponent, parity law, or constant for the balance or compression tax remain open.
